name: Subscribe to This!

pick.label: Pick a subscription
pick.heading: Pick a subscription nobody asked for
lead: These days you can subscribe to almost anything: films, music, razors, flowers, even a new pair of socks every month. People with lots of money and little sense have tried most of them.
Choose something from the shelf (or your own idea) and turn it into a subscription that people would actually sign up for. *And make sure they’re happy to stay.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: Obviously I am not looking for a serious business model here, this is just for a bit of fun. Some subscriptions will make total sense, and some only make sense at two in the morning. Both are welcome.

shelf.head: People
items: A wake-up call from a celebrity
A grandma who checks your homework

rows: What exactly arrives, and how? A box, a visit, a message, something completely mad?
Who signs up first? Students, busy parents, lonely people, someone else?
How much a month, and why is it worth it?
What makes them happy to keep paying, month after month?
Who do you get to talk about it, and where?

values.what: Sock Roulette: one single sock, every month, in a tiny envelope. You lose one sock a month anyway, so now you’re always a sock ahead.
values.who: People like me, who have a drawer full of socks that don’t match and have stopped pretending they ever will.
values.price: €4 a month, which works out at about the price of a coffee in Friedrichshain for something that lasts much longer.
values.stay: Every sock comes with a short, completely made-up story about where its partner went. People stay to find out what happens next.
values.promote: Getting a football commentator to wear odd socks on live TV, then asking everyone to post a photo of their own feet.

yours.label: Your subscription
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your subscription in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which subscription wins?
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their subscription in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
